statement: Faction Influence changes Balance. It is the reading of what a Major Faction controls and how much force it has, not a separate number. A completed Main Goal raises it, and Side Events and Allegiance change the war directly.
rationale: Так 99 закрывает вопрос, что именно двигает Balance, и отсылает к 02.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: The World Engine picks the next faction operation from the World Seed starting state, the current Main Goal, requirements, and eligible Operations.
rationale: Закрыто в 99 и записано в 02. Это не обещание симулировать каждого NPC.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: The player reads Faction Influence through Symptoms, not a meter. Exact stage-to-symptom tables remain open.
rationale: Закрыт способ чтения. Таблица симптомов сознательно не закрыта.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: Only the first character in a new world begins with a Starting Faction. Later characters begin Factionless and earn Faction Entry.
rationale: Записано в 07. Superseded on 2026-11-02: every character starts Uninitiated and Factionless.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: The five decision axes are Attention, Approach, Allegiance, Commitment, and Bargain.
rationale: 99 помечает оси принятыми.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: V1 teaches Attention first, with Approach beside it. Bargain is the second major lesson.
rationale: Записано в 03 по указанию 99.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: An important Decision Node uses at least two axes. A one-axis moment is allowed only as non-major onboarding.
rationale: Записано в 03.1 по указанию 99. Сам шаблон 03.1 в атлас целиком не переносился.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: Side Events are not free bonuses. They are delivered as timed Points of Interest.
rationale: Две закрытые записи 99: содержание события и способ доставки.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: Player Knowledge improves reasoning, places, methods, and prediction. It is not primarily a success-rate bonus.
rationale: Закрыто в 99. Сила Arcana остаётся прогрессией с ценой и Bargain.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: V1 has six Approaches: Confront, Convince, Threaten, Exchange, Veil, and Withdraw. Confront must not have the universal best payoff.
rationale: Имена и запрет лучшей выплаты закрыты. Объём поддержки каждого метода в V1 открыт.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: V1 has three Arcana and only stages 9, 8, and 7. An Arcana is a nudge or a discovery, not a prison. Uninitiated remains valid.
rationale: Закрыто в 99 и записано в 05. Пороги пределов открыты.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: Death ends that Character Life. A fixed short Death Gap follows, Player Knowledge survives, and there is no bloodline power. The length of the gap in days is still open.
rationale: Существование паузы закрыто. Число дней открыто отдельным вопросом.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: A simple V1 Legacy Cache can be prepared on purpose and leaves a map marker for the next life. Ordinary leftovers are not guaranteed.
rationale: Закрыто как возможность. Размер тайника, после которого смерть пустеет, открыт.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: Confront does not grant experience for kills, does not use abstract loot tables, and is not the universal best payoff.
rationale: Ограждение из 08, повторённое в закрытых вопросах 99.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: V1 Confront is turn-based on a thematic Combat Grid. There is no voluntary turn-based mode during free exploration.
rationale: Подача закрыта. Формулы инициативы и цены клетки открыты. Superseded on 2026-11-01 by combat in place.
dateNote: 99 не ставит отдельную дату каждой закрытой записи. Запись уже внесена в Draft.

statement: The spatial lock is a seeded overworld, free third-person movement, separate interiors without a grid, and Confront on an arena.
rationale: 16 называет это запертыми решениями поворота 2026-08-07. Статус файла остаётся Draft. Its arena part was superseded on 2026-11-01 by combat in place.
alternatives: Непрерывная сеточная правда мира, сеточное движение по оверворлду, интерьеры OrganicTown в той же сцене, пошаговый режим на месте и вне боя.
dateNote: Дата поворота, как она названа в 16. Это не отдельный сертификат поверх документа.

statement: The engine for this phase is Unity with URP and C#. Combat Grid combat is custom. Godot 4 was considered and rejected for this phase.
rationale: 12 записывает выбор и отклонённую альтернативу. Отдельную дату в прочитанном фрагменте не беру.
alternatives: Godot 4.
dateNote: Дата в прочитанном фрагменте 12 не указана.

statement: Target geography D6 is approved. It is defined by the owner's concept image and the D6 wording in section 9 of the G2 brief. The image does not supply numeric requirements, and production terrain is unchanged.
rationale: Одобрение цели не является разрешением менять производственный рельеф.
dateNote: Дата одобрения D6, записанная в G2 brief.

statement: OrganicTown and the retired greybox milestone are not sources for the current path.
rationale: 13 и 11.2 помечены Deprecated. 15 прямо запрещает брать 13 как источник. 14 ведёт следующий шаг в Overworld V0.
dateNote: Дата снятия в эту запись не копировалась: статусы документов уже Deprecated.

statement: The Vertical Slice leaves out deep crafting, Death Gap, successor characters, Legacy Cache, World Collapse, and more than two factions.
rationale: Это граница среза, не запрет думать о крафте и наследстве позже.
dateNote: Список прочитан в Scope Out документа 11. Отдельную дату пункта не беру.

statement: Overworld V0 is a 2800 × 2800 m world of 64 m chunks, with a 700 m height budget and sea level at 24 m. Interior V0 load by swapping the whole scene.
rationale: Число прочитано в закрытом блоке 99. Там оно отнесено к 17 и плану Overworld V0; сам план в эту запись заново не сверялся.
dateNote: Дата отдельной строкой в прочитанном блоке 99 не стоит. Запись отнесена к 17 и плану Overworld V0.

statement: World, settlement, building, and interior content is produced by Piece-Based Assembly: small hand-authored pieces snapped together. It is not an algorithmic floor-plan solver and not the retired OrganicTown generator.
rationale: 99 закрывает механизм. Открыт только момент, когда сборка сменяет единственный ручной интерьер V0.
alternatives: Алгоритмический решатель планировок; непрерывный генератор OrganicTown.
dateNote: Дата механизма в прочитанном блоке 99 не выделена.

statement: The first playable proof is a Lower Veil vertical slice with two selectable factions (Wardens / Veinmarket), three POIs, information sources, arena Confront, and one Bargain tease. Placeholder names may change. Death Gap is outside the slice.
rationale: 99 закрывает состав доказательства и прямо разрешает сменить имена-заполнители. Superseded on 2026-11-01 by the one-city slice.
dateNote: Дата строки в прочитанном блоке 99 не стоит.

statement: Item Creation and Enchanting are the only confirmed item-crafting professions; Luck and Perception are attributes, not professions. Separate profession tracks for equipment material families are retired.
rationale: One general Item Creation profession creates all equipment families; Enchanting manipulates modifiers. Luck and Perception affect modifier count but do not create item types or change base weights.

statement: For each of six potential modifier slots, p = min(0.99, (0.10 + 0.60×((ItemCreation−1)/99)) × (1 + 0.10×((Perception−1)/99)) × (1 + Luck/100)); total count is Binomial(6,p). Character factors do not change fixed modifier-type weights.
rationale: Starting balance formula selected under the owner's delegation: Item Creation is the main influence, Perception adds up to 10% relatively, and Luck uses the shared universal probability multiplier.
dateNote: Owner delegated formula and threshold selection 2026-10-31; initial values are subject to later balance testing.

statement: Items may have at most three major and three minor modifiers; group assignment is random, full reforge preserves the existing group distribution, and insertion requires a free slot in the extracted modifier's group.
rationale: This retains the 3+3 structure and disallows insertion when the target group has no capacity.
dateNote: Owner confirmed 2026-10-31; exact random group distribution remains open.

statement: Learning Enchanting grants Step 1; later skill thresholds unlock six cumulative operations in order: random modifier addition, full reforge, locking, extraction/insertion, tier raising, and numeric-value change.
rationale: The owner specified the operation ladder and delegated the initial Item Creation thresholds; numeric Enchanting unlock levels and costs remain open.
dateNote: Owner-confirmed ladder 2026-10-31; exact skill levels remain open.

statement: Extraction destroys its source item and creates one non-copyable modifier instance; one insertion consumes it, preserves identity/tier/group, rerolls numeric value, locks it, and can target any base only if a free slot exists in that modifier's own group. Extraction is allowed from a broken item.
rationale: The modifier is transferred once as a physical instance; insertion is governed by group capacity rather than base compatibility.

statement: At zero durability an item remains present and becomes broken/unusable. Durability applies to hand equipment, worn armour, and resource-gathering tools; jewellery/belts have none. Repair uses some ordinary creation ingredients and no rare ingredient. Broken items cannot be enchanted except for extraction.
rationale: Zero durability changes usability rather than deleting the item; repair does not require rare ingredients; extraction is the sole Enchanting exception for broken items.
dateNote: Owner-confirmed 2026-10-31; wear and repair parameters remain open.

statement: Ordinary monsters drop ingredients only. Each NPC equipped item is independently recoverable at p=min(0.99,0.35×(1+current looter Luck/100)); Perception does not affect the roll. A former player character encountered as a world actor uses the same rule when defeated.
rationale: The 35% base chance and independent item rolls implement the owner's request for a variable NPC recovery amount affected by Luck only; no fixed half or rounding is used.
dateNote: Owner-confirmed loot direction and delegated starting formula 2026-10-31; transformed-NPC-monster drops remain open.

statement: Item Creation skill levels 1, 11, 21, …, 91 unlock item stages 9, 8, 7, …, 0; an item may always be crafted at a lower stage if its materials are supplied.
rationale: Delegated starting thresholds provide ten skill bands aligned with the ten item stages.
dateNote: Selected under owner's delegation 2026-10-31; initial balance may be tuned.

statement: Quality is Normal 0 (grey/desaturated), Magic 1–2 (green), Rare 3 (cyan/light blue), Epic 4 (purple), Legendary 5–6 (yellow-orange); Unique is separate and red. The label changes only when modifier count crosses a category boundary.
rationale: Count bands and color directions are owner-confirmed; exact colour values and UI treatment remain open.

statement: Personal inventory is an unlimited bag with equal-size item entries and no grid/footprint limit; weight is the only carrying limit, and gold weighs zero. Comfortable capacity is 20 kg + Strength, with a hard carry limit at 200% of capacity.
rationale: The owner selected a bag-style interface and delegated starting weights/capacity thresholds.
dateNote: Owner direction and delegated starting balance 2026-10-31.

statement: Every base gives favored modifier types higher fixed weights and all other types lower, nonzero weights; higher item stages increase the weight of stronger tiers without a hard tier ceiling. Character factors do not change the type weights.
rationale: Base tables express preference as probability, while item stage shifts tier probability; no generation-weight preference is a compatibility restriction.
dateNote: Owner-confirmed direction 2026-10-31; exact tables remain open.

statement: The numeric-value operation rerolls the values of all unlocked modifiers, preserving modifier identity, group, and tier; locked modifiers are unchanged.
rationale: This operation changes values only and does not change the modifier set or tier.

statement: A new Character Life does not automatically inherit the prior character's carried/equipped inventory or extracted modifier instances. If the former character exists as a world actor and is defeated, its current equipment uses the ordinary per-item NPC recovery rule; Legacy Cache contents are separate.
rationale: Death does not transfer the prior character's carried inventory. Intentional Legacy Cache eligibility remains a distinct unresolved boundary.
dateNote: Owner-confirmed 2026-10-31; Legacy Cache eligible contents remain open.

statement: The pre-manifestation campaign is a war for cities. At world creation every city is allied; the cult captures cities by conducting rituals in them.
rationale: Gives the threat a public, reversible progress that the player can read and fight.

statement: The Capital Awakening Ritual can begin only when every other city is under Cult Control.
rationale: Replaces the earlier required ritual count and tells the player that the capital is next.

statement: City Capture removes every follower of other factions and holds the city, without attacking ordinary residents. City Liberation is symmetrical.
rationale: Supersedes the earlier civilian-targeted ritual wording.

statement: Three Limit 2 Cult Generals lead the Cult Forces with different styles: the Spirit General, who comes out of the Spirit World only in cities; the Holding General, who stays in a city until it has gathered enough for the next sortie and fights to the end; and the Raiding General, who walks in the open and gathers forces in neutral territory.
rationale: Different enemy behaviour forces different player responses.

statement: Allied forces are generated at world creation and replaced slowly; Cult Forces generate much faster and do not run out until the cult's leadership is destroyed. Campaign pace depends on difficulty.
rationale: Owner's reference is the Dominator pressure curve in Space Rangers 2, as a comparison only.

statement: At the middle difficulty the campaign lasts 15–20 game days, about 40–50 real hours. The target world is 3×3 tiles with 5–7 cities, ideally 7; only cities are cult targets.
rationale: Leaves room for exploration, gathering, monsters, and crafting while the player works with what comes to hand. Replaces D6's 3–5 settlements and changes no production terrain.

statement: Capture rituals turn cities into Places of Power and keep residents alive as sacrifices. Nobody in the world knows this, and the player learns it only at manifestation. At the capital ritual the people in captured cities die; manifestation succeeds only if every city was captured at that moment and the ritual was not interrupted.
rationale: Explains why the cult spares residents and makes the war's real stakes a secret the player can uncover.

statement: Cult followers never hide, attack invaders at once, share a Cult Thought Link, and retreat collectively.
rationale: Closes the single-hidden-follower deadlock for liberation and lets a garrison break without every follower dying.

statement: On every Arcana, including the player's, an occupied Limit 0 leaves no Limit 1, and an unoccupied one allows at most three Limit 1 practitioners. When someone reaches Limit 0, every Limit 1 practitioner of that Arcana moves back to Limit 2. Limit 2 has no limit. A god occupies Limit 0 of one Arcana; a faction's other Arcana may have a free one.
rationale: A world law that prices following a god and explains why the cult and the allied factions stop at Limit 2.

statement: The Divine Plane and the Spirit World are separate. Every Limit 0 being has been on the unreachable Divine Plane since a past cataclysm. The Spirit World is the other side of the real world, reachable by higher followers. The Spirit General lives there, comes out only in cities, and can be defeated only during a capture. The player cannot enter it for now.
rationale: Corrects two earlier readings: the merged places and teleportation across the map. Each General can now be stopped in a different place.

statement: City Capture begins with a Cult Sortie. The ritual runs alongside it: a group goes to the ritual site, guards protect it and then cut off the way, and the main force moves on to the city centre. A garrison stays after the capture.
rationale: Fixes when the player and allies can still intervene.

statement: A ritual stops when everyone conducting it dies, when the senior who started it dies, or, only while the cult has not fully taken the city, when conditions that differ from ritual to ritual are met through persuasion, disguise, and strong dialogue checks. A disrupted ritual lowers the enemy's attributes, and it retreats unless it still dominates by numbers. A new ritual can be held two game days after the previous one.
rationale: Keeps non-combat routes for less warlike Arcana without a learned answer. A fallen city is combat only.

statement: A liberated city goes to the allied faction with the most followers there. A city liberated by the player alone is Unclaimed until an allied follower arrives; that faction's followers then appear there as defenders.
rationale: Ties allied replacement to held cities and gives liberation a concrete result.

statement: Killing all three Cult Generals is the only way to end the campaign before manifestation.
rationale: Replaces the undefined command threshold.

statement: From Limit 5 and deeper a character can change to an adjacent Arcana at a much larger Sanity cost than advancing along their own. Detailed rules come later.
rationale: Gives a way out when a Arcana's Limit 0 is occupied.

statement: Each General launches a Cult Sortie when generation has given it enough followers; no calendar sets attacks. A sortie can fail. At the middle difficulty attackers have the better chance but allies can repel them alone; on harder settings a city almost certainly falls unless someone interferes.
rationale: Tempo emerges from the simulation, with the first sorties around day 3–5.

statement: A new character can appear only while at least one uncaptured city has no battle in it. Otherwise a character's death is final, even before manifestation.
rationale: There is nowhere left to return. Recorded in Canonical 00 Vision and 00.2 Meta Loop as well as 07 and 21.

statement: At manifestation the residents of the capital and of captured cities die. Residents cannot be evacuated, and the ending reports only a few survivors without simulating them.
rationale: A positive ending after manifestation still carries the cost of the sacrifice.

statement: The Vertical Slice is one city and a small territory. The player starts without a faction, may join the internal-order faction through a first-day investigation of a disappearance, finds one or two potions for two styles of play, and reaches Limits 9–8; Limit 7 is for NPCs. The Spirit General comes out on day 1–2, the ritual starts at once, the General leaves after 15–20 ticks, and 8–10 followers hold the ritual for its one-hour window, against allies who stop it about 40 % of the time with no player. The player stops it and wins, or loses; death ends the run. Required in a limited form: exploration, gathering, Item Creation, Alchemy, combat, dialogue with checks, stealth, time, sleep. Out: Enchanting, Death Gap, Legacy Cache, Arcana change.
rationale: The first build should already show the war's core: a General, followers, and a ritual to stop.

statement: An eighth Difficulty Setting, Cult Pace, controls how fast Cult Forces generate followers and so how fast the cult advances.
rationale: It does not fit the other seven sliders, and the rule forbids bundling unrelated effects.

statement: A ritual must be maintained every 24 game hours, so in a liberated city it lapses a game day after the liberation. A defender of Limit 5 or deeper who knows the method undoes it sooner, within 60 ticks of reaching the site. Allied factions have the method, and an outsider earns it through trust as a quest reward.
rationale: A last-minute liberation still does not stop manifestation, and a player with no ally nearby can simply wait the day.

statement: A full city or sortie is about 20 followers of different stages; a city a General has just left holds about 10. The Spirit General generates fastest with weaker followers and strikes first on day 3–5, the Raiding General is in the middle on day 5–7, and the Holding General is slowest on day 7–8.
rationale: Keeps the load reasonable and staggers the first strikes.

statement: A General falls to allied numbers, after a disrupted ritual, or to a character at Limit 2, or Limit 3 with good statistics and strategy. Allied forces can kill Generals without the player: rarely on the middle setting, and all three at the lowest setting, where the game wins by itself.
rationale: There is no special weapon; artifacts are later design.

statement: The game has 22 Arcana, one for each Tarot Major Arcana archetype, and each has ten Limits tied to the ten Sephiroth, with 220 names in all. A character is an Arcana, a Limit, and that Limit's name. There are no separate paths or path names. Each Arcana has two primary attributes and one secondary attribute.
rationale: Gives advancement a shared structure; each Arcana still has to differ by way of acting.

statement: Each Limit grants two abilities, passive or active, combat or exploration, in a mix that differs by Arcana, and raises the Arcana's primary attributes. NPCs use the same abilities, so a Limit 7 NPC has about six.
rationale: Fixed for the slice and may change later.

statement: The internal-order faction has the High Priestess, with an occupied Limit 0, and the Fool and Magician, with a free one. The cult has the Emperor, occupied by the sealed being, and the Empress and Hierophant, occupied by sane gods who want to use the True God's descent.
rationale: Shows a faction's god holding only one of its Arcana.

statement: Confront runs in place on a Combat Grid that forms around the player from real geometry reaches 20 cells in every direction, and follows the player every step; fights the player cannot see are simulated by tick without a grid. The Combat Arena and Theme Packs are retired. Interiors stay separate scenes with their own grid, and a fight follows through a door like a level change in Fallout. A round is one tick. Walls that block the view become transparent outlines. The grid is built during a real fight, at 20 cells in the slice, with 50 cells planned for later.
rationale: Owner's intended combat. It restores in-location Turn-Based Mode, which was cancelled in 2026-08 as too expensive; the grid exists only during Confront.

statement: The slice's Arcana are Жрица, offered by the faction for dialogue and stealth, and Император, found alone for confrontation. A character on Император must seek the next Limit among the cultists. Both have an occupied Limit 0.
rationale: Makes joining or going alone a choice of play style with a lasting cost.

statement: A ritual lasts one in-game hour: 60 ticks, ten real minutes of free exploration, or up to 60 rounds in a fight.
rationale: Replaces the earlier six-hour window; one in-game hour suits the expected battle length.

statement: While Turn-Based Mode runs, everything outside the fight stands still and lives one tick at the end of each round. Ordinary NPCs hide, and defenders who can fight go to it. A character leaves the fight about 10 cells from the nearest enemy.
rationale: Unlike Baldur's Gate 3, the world keeps one clock.

statement: Battles should last about as long as an army battle in Heroes of Might and Magic III or Olden Era, and NPCs act quickly by fixed rules.
rationale: Keeps fights of 15–20 combatants playable.

statement: An Arcana's secondary attribute is fixed. It does not change by Limit or by World Seed.
rationale: Replaces the earlier per-seed rule.

statement: The ritual and the capture are two tracks. Allies know a ritual is running and roughly where, but their directive is the main force first, because a ritual has no victims. Only the player can choose to go for the ritual first, and the capital's final battle is the one exception: part of the defenders meets the ritual from the start. A Cult Retreat ends a running ritual: the order reaches every follower at once, and those conducting it leave without fighting.
rationale: Keeps stealth and dialogue as answers while a defence without the player can still stop the ritual at the middle difficulty.

statement: Every group, cult or allied, decides whether to fight from a Force Estimate over the strength of each side, as in Heroes of Might and Magic and Space Rangers 2. Defenders may flee or stay out of a hopeless fight. Cult followers flee only when it is very strongly against them, and fight on if retreat has no chance either. A senior's death or a disrupted ritual counts only through the strength it changes.
rationale: A lone surviving ally does not end a ritual, and the cult's choices follow from its asymmetric recovery.

statement: Cover works only against ranged attacks, magical or by weapon, because it is a problem of aiming. It gives no advantage in melee. A fence is Half Cover, a small hindrance. Trees are obstacles and cover, and fences, boundaries, lamps, props, and trees get colliders.
rationale: Keeps cover readable and gives melee a reason to close the distance.

statement: Every character starts Uninitiated and Factionless, in the slice and the full game. All seven attributes start at 1, and the player spends 9 free points or picks an 11-point Character Archetype: Боец, Сыщик, or Оборванец. In the full game archetypes are assembled from templates by seed.
rationale: Keeps Allegiance earned in every life and leaves room for seeded starts later.

statement: The slice has 12 abilities, six each for Жрица and Император at Limits 9–7. Cult followers use only Император and allies only Жрица. A failed ability spends its Will Power and has its own consequence; an ability aimed at the character has a drawback instead of a check.
rationale: Failure stays valuable, and one set of abilities covers both sides of the slice.

statement: A full sleep restores a little Sanity, replacing the earlier rule that sleep restores none. Reaching zero Will Power takes a little Sanity.
rationale: Sanity stays a long pressure without being a one-way loss within a campaign.

statement: A Limit raises each primary attribute by +3, +4, +5, +6, +7, +8, +8, +9, +9, +10 from Limit 9 to Limit 0, and the secondary by +1, +2, +2, +2, +2, +3, +3, +3, +3, +3.
rationale: Deep Limits feel stronger while training stays needed at every step and the total fits the 1–100 scale.
alternatives: About 30 % of the target Limit's band, which totals 165 and removes training from Limit 5.

statement: Stealth is a special action. NPCs have 10-cell Vision Cones whose angle Vigilance sets, and a Notice Meter fills by Stealth skill and Dexterity against Perception. Darkness adds to Stealth skill, and noise is not simulated. Perception shows the meter and Intelligence the cones. An NPC that loses sight of the character checks the last place and stays Alert. Outside a fight allies break stealth too. A stealth attack rolls to hit as usual, adds 50 percentage points of critical chance, and never stuns.
rationale: Gives Veil real rules, ties what the player can read to attributes, and keeps striking from hiding from answering every fight.
alternatives: Single checks of Dexterity against Perception, which are simpler but opaque.

statement: In combat, critical chance above the 95 % cap adds to the critical damage multiplier one to one, so an excess of 0.50 adds 0.5.
rationale: A bonus past the cap keeps its worth, and a stealth attack rewards high Perception with harder hits instead of nothing.
alternatives: Discarding the excess, which 07.1 already rejected.

statement: Dialogue follows Disco Elysium: 2d6 + Character Value + Modifiers against Request + Listener Value, +2 for an enemy. A Social Check exists only with an Argument the character gained in this life. Persuasion and Deception use Intelligence and Will, Intimidation uses Strength and Will, and the listener resists with the same attributes. Persuasion brings an ordinary gain, and Deception brings more and costs more. A failed check is not repeated on the spot: friendly listeners may give a clue or a Proof Task, and against enemies it is a Final Check that ends in a fight. Reputation and Danger are read from a Deeds Record.
rationale: Knowledge opens a conversation instead of stats, a flatter two-dice curve keeps a small lead from winning every talk, and a failure changes the situation instead of wasting time.
alternatives: The shared curve of 07.1, which reaches 99 % at a lead of 4 and falls to 1 % at a difference of 8.

statement: A ritual in the slice has two Ritual Weak Points, chosen by the seed from Сомневающийся, Посланник, Грязная тайна, and Основа ритуала. Any one stops it. No list or map mark shows them: the player recognises one on finding its Argument. A failed Final Check leaves only the hidden route, and the followers report it through the Cult Thought Link, which carries orders and reports in exceptional cases.
rationale: Gives a non-violent way to win that rests on what the character found out, differs each run, and uses stealth, Alchemy, and the three Social Checks.
alternatives: One fixed answer per ritual, which a player learns once; or map marks, which remove the search.

statement: Any dialogue pauses the world, with no exceptions, and costs one tick when it ends.
rationale: Keeps one simple rule, spares the player from hurrying through lines, and matches a combat round, which is untimed and costs one tick.
alternatives: A tick per line at a running ritual, which needs an exception.

statement: Combat Numbers V0 are authoring defaults in 10.2 §5b: 70 % base hit, Accuracy against Evasion, 10 AP plus Dexterity / 20, weapons from 3 AP to 7 AP, defence / (defence + 50) reduction capped at 75 %, and a Will Contest from 50 %. In the slice the ritual group is a Limit 8 senior and two Limit 9 conductors, a Limit 7 follower leads the main force, and the 5 allies are two of Limit 9 and three of Limit 8. The two allied Limit 9 fighters and one cult Limit 9 fighter have rifles, and a cult fighter has +1 over an allied fighter of the same Limit.
rationale: The owner left balance calculations to the agent. A simulation gives even duels between peers and even weapons, and on the Combat Grid it gives the allies alone a 40 % chance of stopping the ritual, while an open assault on the ritual fails.
alternatives: A Limit 7 senior at the ritual, which leaves the best plan at 3 %.
dateNote: Authoring defaults calculated on the owner's instruction, 2026-11-02.

statement: A conductor who fights goes on conducting and has 3 AP less each turn. The ritual does not stop because someone was attacked.
rationale: The fight at the circle stays worth starting, and the ritual keeps running while it lasts.
alternatives: Conductors at full AP, which makes the fight harder still, or half AP, which leaves a two-handed senior unable to attack.

statement: Traces of a Ritual Weak Point were left by people who joined the General earlier, not by a hidden agent. Each Weak Point has two sources in the city and one during the invasion; any one opens it, and each further one adds +1. Only the run's two Weak Points leave traces, the first-day trial always leads past one, witnesses hide when the invasion starts, and a real Посланник does not appear in the slice.
rationale: One source explains all four kinds and keeps the rule that followers never hide. Several sources stop a single clue from blocking a route, and a first run still shows that the option exists.
alternatives: A hidden cult agent in the city, or false traces.

statement: Found facts go into Character Notes: short records with no hint of what they are for. They hold facts, not goals or solutions.
rationale: The player keeps what was found without a quest journal that replaces reading the world.
alternatives: No record at all, or a quest journal.

statement: Campaign Numbers V0 are authoring defaults in 21 §8, checked by a simulation of a whole war with no player, up to manifestation or the death of all three Generals. Off-screen fights run tick by tick over a per-city ledger of followers per Limit, using a kill table from Combat Numbers V0, and the Force Estimate is the square-law ratio over that table. Cult Pace runs from ×0.5 to ×1.5 in five steps, and a working ladder of five presets moves it with Combat Difficulty.
rationale: At the middle setting they give 42 % allied wins and 57 % cult wins over 3000 wars, a median war of 19 days, and 5.2 liberation attempts per war. A table replaces a single strength value because hit chances are capped.
alternatives: A single strength value per Limit, which cannot express large Limit gaps, or a full tactical simulation of every unseen fight.
dateNote: Authoring defaults, 2026-11-02. The owner leaves balance calculations to the agent.

statement: Simulations never count the player. With no player the allied side wins at low settings, the middle setting is 40/60 in favour of the cult, higher settings are 20/80 and worse, and the slice is about 40/60 with no easier or harder variant for now. Only the player's actions can turn this.
rationale: The war must press the player to take part, and the player's gear, progression, and choices must be what decides it.
alternatives: Odds near even at the middle setting, which leave the player's help optional.

statement: Allied factions act on goals as enemy NPCs do: they choose a city and forces, reinforce a city under attack, retake cities while their forces allow, and hold the capital, so only a pool of forces is free. They post Liberation Contracts, have Limit 2 Allied Generals, and their goddess can give a Divine Blessing now and then.
rationale: A one-sided war teaches nothing and gives the player no battles to join. Both sides must pursue their goals with the same seriousness.
alternatives: A fixed allied reinforcement and a daily share of spare forces, the first simulation, which left the allies nearly passive.
dateNote: Owner decision, 2026-11-02. Its numbers are working readings.

statement: Faction Influence is not a separate number. City Control and the followers in each city are the state, and a Side Event changes that state directly. Minor Factions and local groups have no Influence of their own.
rationale: The war and the older Influence model were two unconnected accounts. One state means Side Events matter to the war and the simulation can test them.
alternatives: Retiring Influence, which leaves Balance as lore and takes away the hidden residue of Side Events; keeping both layers, which is the most expensive for a solo project.

statement: NPCs close in on the nearest targets, a melee fighter tries for the shooters and attacks whoever it reaches on the way, and each side goes first for whoever brings the most to the fight and can actually be harmed. Working form: Target Impact and Held in 10.2 §5a.
rationale: With no positions a fight is a race of total damage, and one more body decides it. The owner wants strategic decisions on both sides and enemies a little stronger than allies.
alternatives: Nearest target only, which plays worse; machine-learning AI, which the owner ruled out.
dateNote: Direction owner-approved, 2026-11-02; numbers are working readings.

statement: A thrown potion that deals magical damage on 3 × 3 cells and hits allies too, carried by the two deepest fighters of a group.
rationale: Of the rules tried on the Combat Grid only an attack on an area, kept with deep Limits, made one more fighter weigh little: +7 points for a club and +11 for a Limit 9, against +31 and +32 before.
alternatives: Whole sets of items, which the owner chose: see d-items-in-fights.
dateNote: Proposed and rejected by the owner, 2026-11-02.

statement: Attributes differ only slightly and soldiers have a random spread. Whole sets of items decide fights and strengthen a character significantly. No single item or consumable may change a battle's result that much. The allies' edge in items stays with their Limit 8 fighters.
rationale: The owner rejected a flask that did 58 % of a battle's damage and wants fights played through items. With Outfit V0 the allies alone stay near 40 %, one more club adds 12 points against 29 with no items, and one Rare weapon on one fighter adds about 2.
alternatives: Attributes ×2 or ×3, which the owner refused; the Alchemical Flask, rejected.
dateNote: Direction owner-approved, 2026-11-02; values are authoring defaults, CC-47.

statement: Every city has shops kept by Masters who teach their professions. Both sides buy in them, so no armourers exist. Shelves improve with the age of the world, and joining a faction may bring a Faction Gift.
rationale: The owner wants items to need no separate explanation. Because the shops are shared, every shop +20 moves the slice by only 2 points, so the world cannot tilt one side's supply.
alternatives: Armourers for each side, withdrawn by the owner.
dateNote: Direction owner-approved, 2026-11-02; Shop Skill values are authoring defaults, CC-48.

statement: A fighter can wait to the end of the round, and those who waited act lowest Initiative first; NPCs use it. Instead of attacking, a fighter can take a Defensive Stance and answer with a Counterattack, which must not become a best move. Critical hits are ×2.
rationale: Going first used to lose fights, at 26 %, and a set of critical hits was the weakest. With Waiting and Hold Back, Initiative wins 60 %, and a critical set 42-45 %. A fighter who only stands in a stance wins 38 %, or 49 % with a shield.
alternatives: A Counterattack with no extra AP, where standing still with a shield won 64 %.
dateNote: Rules owner-approved, 2026-11-02; values are authoring defaults, and Hold Back is a working reading.

statement: Critical, attack, magic, and shooter builds are about equal overall and play against each other: mages beat plate, plate beats shooters, shooters beat mages. Initiative is no automatic win. The weapons are Victorian and iron: dagger, sword, axe, mace, greatsword, greataxe, and maul, each with its own trait, and rifles and pistols whose shot includes loading, 6 AP for a rifle and 4 for a pistol, with no Reload, the shooter stepping back with the AP left; staffs, wands, bows, and crossbows are out. A firearm goes only with a Cartridge Pouch of infinite cartridges, and a character carries two Weapon Sets. A Point-Blank Shot only aims worse, with no doubled armour, and Melee Skill and Ranged Skill are separate. Cloth gives mostly magical defence, leather half and half, and plate physical defence only. V1 counts no ammunition, by the owner's choice on 2026-11-03. With a melee set shooters and mages win about half their duels, accepted by the owner on 2026-11-03. An ally can wake a sleeper; Дрёма costs 2 AP and waking 6 AP, and Не сдвинуть is paid from the AP left at the end of a turn, never from a blow. The slice at 23 % with no player is accepted, by the owner on 2026-11-03.
rationale: With two Weapon Sets for every build, a shot with no Reload, stepping back, Infusion at Intelligence / 24, the rifle's base at 6.75, and the pistol's at 5, the five builds reach 46-54 % five against five, and the triangle stands at 75, 71, and 79, about 70 % a side by the owner's direction. Physical defence counts double against ranged physical damage beyond the next cell, and load bands make Strength pay for heavy armour. A shooter who changes to a sword at point blank has a mean of 50, against 34 for one who keeps the rifle. Investing in Initiative costs a build 10-13 points.
alternatives: A fixed Evasion or AP penalty on plate: AP was too sharp, because one AP took a second blow away from a one-handed fighter, and neither stopped a mage or a shooter from wearing it.
dateNote: Direction owner-approved, 2026-11-02; weakness alone, no ammunition in V1, no bows, the armour split, waking a sleeper, kinds of weapon, the Cartridge Pouch, and two Weapon Sets owner-approved, 2026-11-03; the triangle at about 70 %, the Point-Blank Shot, and separate weapon skills by the owner's direction, 2026-11-03; Не сдвинуть on end-of-turn AP owner-approved, 2026-11-03; values are authoring defaults, CC-49; a shot with no Reload and stepping back owner-approved, 2026-11-03.

statement: A melee attack goes across a cell's side only. Leaving the side of an enemy holding a melee weapon draws its free Reaction Attack, once a round from each enemy, with no Infusion or ability. Two or more enemies beside a character make it Surrounded, +10 or +20 to hit, so fights need no facing.
rationale: The Reaction Attack makes position matter and moves the builds by at most 2 points. Surrounded pays melee fighters for standing together: without it plate falls from 56 to 46.
alternatives: Held, a step that cost 2 AP more, which gave about the same numbers; flank and rear bonuses, which needed facing.

statement: A character fills a weapon with magic through Will Power: at a flat cost paid for each blow, never once a turn, it adds magical damage set by Intelligence. It works with any weapon and needs no spell. Any initiated character can infuse, with no training. Zero Will Power through it is ordinary exhaustion, with its reward. Magical weapons give the same damage with no Will Power. Crafting has no ceiling, and its price is time and effort.
rationale: Characters of high Intelligence use the same items as everyone else and repay weak Strength and Dexterity this way. The cost is flat so that more Will means more blows, and plate's low magical defence makes the blow armour-piercing. Allies who do not infuse fall from 41 % to 34 % in the slice.
alternatives: A cost as a share of maximum Will Power, which would give more Will no more blows. Staffs and wands, cancelled by the owner.
dateNote: Direction owner-approved, 2026-11-02; any initiated character, with no training, a price for each blow, and ordinary exhaustion, owner-approved, 2026-11-03; values are working readings, CC-49.
